- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

steps.text: Write the live-change@1 contract: change event shape (namespace, key, op upsert|delete|reorder, rev, origin session/surface, ts), resume-from-rev semantics, and the rule that the grid keeps scroll, selection, sort, filters and open dialogs. Spec doc plus its entry in the schema registry.

Reference engine framework/core/engines/live-rows.ts: apply a batch of change events to a keyed row set and return the changed keys only (upsert, delete, reorder, rev gaps → needs resync). Pure TS, no React.
Optimistic layer in live-rows.ts: pending local ops by client op id, show them at once, reconcile when the server echo arrives (match by op id), roll back with a reason on reject or timeout.

Golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/live-rows.json (apply, reorder, delete, gap → resync, optimistic confirm, optimistic rollback) via gen-fixtures; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

axf-data change feed: every data-store@1 write appends a live-change@1 event (namespace, key, op, rev, origin) to an in-memory ring with a monotonic rev; GET /changes?since=<rev>&ns=… returns the backlog.
axf-data SSE endpoint /changes/stream (namespace filter, Last-Event-ID resume, heartbeat every 15 s, backlog replay after a reconnect); unit test.

Console server relay: data_store.py subscribes to the axf-data feed (polling fallback while axf-data is down) and re-serves it at GET /api/live/stream with console auth, so the browser has one stream.

Builds store and lander emit too: builds-store.mjs writes, builds-live.mjs and the VPS lander/merge-queue state writes publish change events (namespace builds, landing-line, merge-queue) through data-files.mjs, so CLI, MCP, voice and VPS changes reach the stream.

Framework client framework/react/live/LiveFeed.ts: one shared EventSource per app, auto-reconnect with backoff, resume by last rev, full resync on a gap, state connected|reconnecting|offline exposed as a hook useLiveFeed().
useLiveRows(namespace, keyOf, load) hook on the live-rows engine: initial load, apply events, return rows plus changedKeys; mutate(op) helper for optimistic local actions with server reconcile.

DataGrid live mode: a `live` prop (namespace + key) re-renders only changed rows (memoised rows keyed by id), keeps scroll position, selection, sort, filters and open dialogs; brief changed-row flash from a theme token (no hardcoded colours).
Lists and tables get the same: the framework list/table components take `live` too, and drag-and-drop reorder in DataGrid/lists goes through mutate() so the drop shows instantly and reconciles.
Live indicator: banner status widget (connected / reconnecting / offline, last event time) as an asset-driven chip registered with the banner frame, plus a per-grid dot; tokens only.

Live API parity: GET /api/live/state (connection, rev, subscribers per namespace), POST /api/live/resync; console actions live.state / live.resync / live.show; MCP tools via plugin-commands; `axf live state|resync|tail`; AmberX voice phrases; console_show target view for the indicator; register control@1 targets (append-only).
Wire the Build orchestrator tabs and Pending list to live mode (namespace builds); drag-reorder in the queue and Auto-lander rows use mutate().
Wire Auto-lander / merge queue grid (landing-line, merge-queue namespaces), including drag-to-set merge order, optimistic with reconcile.
Wire Plan Studio and UI Review grids (plan-studio, ui-review namespaces); archive/edit actions optimistic.

Sweep the remaining console grids/lists (Codebase changes, Screenshots, Breakroom, Plugin Manager…) onto live mode; add a CI check that fails a DataGrid over store data without `live` (ratchet baseline that only goes down).
Re-bake the framework into the console and other shared apps (rebake.mjs), run theme-swap, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, check-chrome-assets; fix findings.

Tests: live-rows fixtures check, axf-data stream test, an end-to-end test that a CLI store write shows in an open grid with scroll and selection kept and that it reconnects after a server restart; UI Review submit with 3 indicator options as assets; report _claude/builds/reports/live-hot-refresh-every-grid-list-re.md (incl. how each part is reached: REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link); THREADS row; PR.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step rebuild-fresh-main-phone-connect-small <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note rebuild-fresh-main-phone-connect-small "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- Android kernel is pure Kotlin (no Android imports). Platform specifics go behind kernel seams. Packages are `ai.amberx.axf.*`, Maven coordinates are `ai.amberx.axf:<module>:<version>`.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). steps.text: Write the ui-state@1 contract: per-user server-side store for settings, asset overrides (axf.chrome.*), layout, dock, columns, tabs and last route; key shape, scopes (user/device-free), versioning, conflict rule (last save wins per key), migration-from-browser marker, and reset semantics. Add the ui-state@1 schema + reference engine (pure: merge per key, prefix reset such as `axf.chrome.*`, diff, export/import, migration plan from a browser key dump with a deny list for secrets/session tokens) and golden fixtures.

Add a server-backed storage seam to the framework settings layer: SettingsRegistry gets a pluggable backend (memory cache + async server sync), localStorage stays only as a fallback for apps with no server; refreshFromSaved reads from the backend. Record the Android twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.

Add a framework `useUiState(key, default)` hook and a `uiStateBackend` that writes through the seam, and replace the framework's own direct localStorage reads/writes (ChromeContext per-asset axf.chrome.* settings, TabGroup remember-last-tab, tapConfirm settings, dock/column helpers) with it.

Server side: ui_state store in the console server through data_store.py (namespace ui-state/<user>), per-user from the hub session; REST routes GET/PUT/PATCH /api/ui-state, DELETE /api/ui-state?prefix=, POST /api/ui-state/migrate (one-time browser upload, idempotent, marks user as migrated).
Server tests for ui-state routes: per-user isolation, last-save-wins per key, prefix reset, migrate idempotent, secret keys refused, works with axf-data down via the data-store shadow rules.

Inventory every localStorage/sessionStorage use in the console app and plugins (grep), write the key list with owner and target ui-state key into a checked-in map, and add a CI check `check-no-browser-storage.mjs` that fails on new direct localStorage use outside the framework fallback (ratchet baseline).

Console boot: install the server ui-state backend in AxfProvider for the console, load the user's state before first paint (landing screen waits), and run the one-time migration: collect existing axf.* browser keys, POST /api/ui-state/migrate, then clear them from localStorage on success.
Move console layout, dock, window positions and grid column state (widths, order, hidden, sort) from localStorage to useUiState.
Move the console's plugin settings and remaining UI state (banner prefs, terminal tabs, nav collapse, follow chips, misc plugin keys from the inventory, first half) to useUiState.
Move the second half of plugin keys from the inventory to useUiState and bring the browser-storage baseline to zero for the console (sessionStorage auth tokens stay, listed as allowed with reason).

Reload keeps your place: save current route, tab, open dialog and its target to ui-state `console.lastLocation` on every navigation (using the console-control address), restore it on load instead of Home; deep links in the URL still win.
Make the URL carry the location too (hash/query with view, tab, dialog) so a browser reload and shared links land on the same spot; register targets with console-control.

Settings → Appearance: add 'Reset every asset override' (clears all axf.chrome.* for this user, confirm + one undo) and show the live count of controlled assets from server state; register as console-control target.

API parity for reset + state: console actions `ui-state.get`, `ui-state.set`, `ui-state.reset` (prefix), `chrome.reset-all`, `console.last-location`; MCP tools, `axf ui-state get|set|reset|overrides` CLI and AmberX voice phrases, all on the same REST routes; deep link view:settings/tab:appearance#asset-overrides.

after.title: Pending optimizer: AI finds pending builds that should be one and combines them
after.detail: An AI pass (on demand, plus automatically when a build is filed) goes through every Pending build, finds the ones that touch the same files, features or contracts (or would clash / redo each other) and proposes combining them. Combining makes one new build that keeps every step of the originals (done steps stay done, in order, with Brett's original words for each), and archives the originals with a link to the combined one. Builds that already have done steps on separate branches are only combined after their branches are merged together cleanly; otherwise they're flagged, not combined. Shows its reasoning per group; Brett can approve all, approve per group, or switch it to auto. Full API parity (deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI, voice). Tests + UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: make it a plain script on the VPS (zero tokens), not AI. It groups and combines builds by overlap of the files, plugins, contracts and settings keys their steps list. The optimizer's job is to never let two builds undo or clash with each other: anything overlapping gets combined. AI only as an optional extra pass, off by default.
Brett: put an Optimize button on Pending, with a small 'Use Claude' switch right next to it. Off = the plain script (zero tokens). On = Claude does the grouping. Same switch over REST/MCP/CLI/voice.

Brett: next to the 'Use Claude' switch, a small '?' tooltip icon explaining it: off = free script that combines builds touching the same files; on = Claude decides (costs tokens, catches builds that would undo each other in different files).
Split by Claude into 20 steps (5 Fable).

Brett: optimizer limits as preference settings: max projected work per combined build (estimated minutes, default 3 h), plus max steps and max projected tokens as backstops, whichever hits first. The optimizer is a dialog (Optimize button + Use Claude switch + ? tooltip + these limits) that pops up from hooks in the application menu, the context menu and the Pending toolbar.

origin.said: It'd have to be AI that will optimize pending. It will take all the jobs that should be made one and combine them. It will go through all the pending builds, figure out which ones can be combined or should be, and optimize that and merge them all into their own build with the same steps that existed in the individual builds.

steps.text: Design the pending-merge@1 contract: the shape of a combine proposal (group id, member build ids, reasoning, overlap evidence: files/features/contracts/clash kind, confidence, blockers) and of a combine result (new combined build, step order, each step keeping its source build id, done state and that build's origin.said; originals archived with combinedInto link). Write framework/spec/PENDING-MERGE.md and add the JSON schema.

Extend builds@1 for combining: add optional combinedInto / combinedFrom / archived status and per-step sourceBuild + sourceSaid fields; keep them through normBuild (it drops unknown fields today) and through the journal and exports; bump the store's migration so old records still load unchanged.

Keep Brett's words through a combine: build-origin@1 gets a combined form (one origin per source build, in order, plus an addendum naming the merge) so the combined build shows every original said block and none is paraphrased; update the origins.json sidecar merge.

Write the pure combine core framework/core/pending-merge.mjs: combine(builds[]) → new build (steps concatenated per source in filed order, done steps stay done and ticked, ids remapped without collision, priority = highest of the group, estimates summed) and archive patches for the originals. No I/O.

Branch guard in the core: a member with done steps on its own branch can only be combined when every such branch merges cleanly with the others (git merge-tree check via an injected git reader); otherwise the group is returned as flagged with the clash files, never combined. Add a reversal (uncombine) that restores the originals from the journal.

Golden fixture and spec check: framework/spec/fixtures/pending-merge.json (plain combine, done steps kept, origins kept, branch clash flagged, uncombine restores) and framework/spec/check-pending-merge.mjs; wire into the CI sweep.

Cheap candidate finder (no AI): score every Pending pair by overlapping files/areas in steps, shared feature/plugin names, contract and schema names, and the clash/redo words already noted on builds; cluster into candidate groups. Pure function in framework/core/pending-optimizer.mjs.

AI pass: framework/cli/pending-optimizer.mjs analyse sends each candidate group (titles, steps, files, Brett's words) to one Opus call through the existing llm capability, gets back yes/no, merged title and plain reasoning per group, and writes proposals (pending-merge@1) to the data store namespace plugins/build-orchestrator/optimizer via data-files.mjs. Cache per group hash so an unchanged group is not re-asked.

Apply path in the CLI: pending-optimizer.mjs apply <group|--all>, dismiss <group>, uncombine <build>, mode manual|auto, status; apply runs the branch guard, then writes the combined build and archives the originals under the store lock (one journalled write), and calls builds-live so it reaches main.

Auto trigger: when a build is filed into Pending (build-hook@1 created / steps-added after pipeline intake split), run the finder for groups that include it, then the AI pass; in auto mode apply clean groups at once, in manual mode leave proposals and raise one notification through axf.notify@1 (declare it in notify.json).
Settings: optimizer mode (manual / auto), auto-run on filing (on), minimum confidence, max groups per run; add them to the plugin settings registry with defaults and levels (level toolbar).

Server routes in the build-orchestrator plugin: GET optimizer/state, GET optimizer/proposals, POST optimizer/run, POST optimizer/apply (group or all), POST optimizer/dismiss, POST optimizer/uncombine, PUT optimizer/mode; all call the CLI core; mode switch to auto respects the settings policy.

MCP + plugin commands + voice: register pending-optimizer_state / _run / _apply / _dismiss / _uncombine / _mode as plugin commands (MCP picks them up), AmberX voice actions ("optimize pending", "combine group …", "approve all combines"), and axf CLI alias `axf pending optimize …`.

Console UI: Optimizer tab in Builds → Pipeline (framework TabGroup + DataGrid): one card per group with members, overlap evidence, AI reasoning, flagged reason for branch clashes; toolbar (role=toolbar) with Run now, Approve all, mode switch; per-group Approve / Dismiss. Tokens and framework controls only.

Combined build view: on a combined build show its source builds (links), each step's source tag and Brett's words per source; on an archived original show 'Combined into <build>' with a link and Uncombine (confirm). Pending list hides archived builds by default with a filter to show them.

Deep links and console control: register targets view:builds/tab:pipeline=optimizer, row:optimizer/<group>, its buttons and the mode setting with data-axf-target (append-only in control@1); console_show / console_open open a group; run check-console-control.mjs.

Plugin tests: python route tests (state, run with a stubbed llm, apply, branch-clash flagged, uncombine, mode) and a node test for the auto trigger on filing; help stub and glossary descriptions for the new commands.

Run the full checks (check-pending-merge, check-builds-store, builds-store verify, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, console typecheck + build), fix anything red, commit.

UI Review: shoot the Optimizer tab and the combined-build view on desktop and phone with seeded Pending builds, ship 3 layout options as assets in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/, submit with review.mjs submit --choices.

Tests green, write _claude/builds/reports/pending-optimizer-ai-finds-pending.md (what it does, API parity: deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI, voice for each action and setting; tests), add the THREADS row, push the branch, open the PR saying how each feature is reached and that UI Review is waiting, link it with builds-live.mjs link.

# Build: rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-17T18:56:41.307Z
> Everywhere there's a toolbar, rebuild the asset for that page/plugin with useful, integrated buttons made for it. Use Fable.

## What to build
Continue build "Rebuild every toolbar with page-specific buttons (Fable)" (rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-17 18:56):
"Everywhere there's a toolbar, rebuild the asset for that page/plugin with useful, integrated buttons made for it. Use Fable."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (7 left, ~1.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Inventory every toolbar (not tab groups): run framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs and grep role="toolbar" / data-axf-toolbar in apps/console-web/src, apps/console-web/plugins, apps/molly, apps/amberx-droid web, apps/expenses and framework/react. Write _claude/builds/reports/rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific/inventory.json listing each toolbar's settings id, page/plugin, current buttons and that page's real functions (from its routes, actions and plugin commands). Commit.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Design the page-toolbar contract: extend the toolbar entry in framework/schemas/asset-types.json so a toolbar asset can be bound to a page or plugin (scope: view:<id> | plugin:<id>) and its buttons can bind to an action ref (console action, plugin command, control@1 target or a framework-registered handler) with enabledWhen/visibleWhen state keys, a badge source, a destructive flag, an optional confirm, groups and overflow. Keep the old shape valid. Regenerate schemas with axf.mjs schemas. Commit.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Migration design: write framework/core/engines/toolbar-migrate.mjs, which moves old toolbar assets (bare button lists) onto the new shape with no visible change. Add it to the validators (axf.mjs validate) and add a fixture case. Commit.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Reference engine: framework/core/engines/toolbar-actions.ts resolves a page toolbar asset into ready buttons (action ref → invoker, enabled/visible from page state, badges, overflow order, merge with the per-toolbar user settings from tapconfirm/toolbar settings). Export it from framework/core. Commit.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Conformance fixtures: generate framework/spec/fixtures/toolbar-actions.json with gen-fixtures.mts (migration, state gating, overflow, scope match) and add a check, framework/spec/check-toolbar-actions.mts. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md (Android on hold). Commit.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Framework React: let framework/react Toolbar render from a page toolbar asset through the engine (usePageToolbar(viewId) hook, page state provider, action dispatch through console actions / plugin commands), keeping role="toolbar", aria-label, tap-to-confirm, the context menu (Settings… / Change… / Move) and dropped hooks. Tokens only. Commit.
[ ] s7 (~10 min) API spine for every page toolbar: register each toolbar and button as console-control targets (toolbar:<id>, toolbar:<id>/button:<b>) with state readable, then add the REST routes GET/POST /api/console-control toolbar list|get|press, MCP console_control toolbar tools, CLI `axf console toolbar list|get|press` and AmberX voice phrases. Append-only in the control@1 registry. Commit.
Read first: framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs, _claude/builds/reports/rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific/inventory.json, framework/schemas/asset-types.json, framework/schemas/json/, framework/core/engines/toolbar-migrate.mjs, framework/cli/axf.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/, framework/core/engines/toolbar-actions.ts, framework/core/index.ts, framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts, framework/spec/fixtures/toolbar-actions.json, framework/spec/check-toolbar-actions.mts, framework/spec/PORTING.md, framework/react/components/Toolbar.tsx, framework/react/pageToolbar.ts, framework/react/tapConfirm.ts, framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md, apps/console-web/server/, framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note rebuild-every-toolbar-page-specific "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.

CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).

Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.

Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.

Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
