The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Every notification is in the one registry (Nov 6 2026, Brett: "I need to control all the notifications."): every notification goes through the console's alert hub or asks capability `axf.notify@1` before it sends; a plugin that sends one declares it in its own `notify.json` (`notify-types@1`), and the Notifications panel controls it (Plugins → Notifications; `axf notify-control …`, MCP `notify-control_*`). Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

steps.text: Design the build-live@1 event contract: the build change and liveness events pushed over the console live channel (build id, status, step, alive/stale/dead, cause, exit code, last step, what the watchdog is doing, at). Write the spec, JSON schema and a golden fixture. Coordinate with the #772 recovery and #780 stale-row watchdogs: liveness reuses their verdicts and adds no check of its own.

Add the reference engine framework/core/engines/build-live.mjs: fold events into a per-build live state (running, alive, stale, broke, done), work out when a row counts as broken, and dedupe repeated events. Add its fixture check.

Register a new asset type, run-indicator (asset@1): the animation (flash, pulse, glow, spin, none), the icon, the running and broke tones as theme token refs, speed and duration, the reduced-motion fallback and a skin declaration. Add it to asset-types.json before uac-policy, regenerate the JSON Schemas and record the deferred Android twin in PORTING.md.

Add the run-indicator engine that compiles the asset into --fx-run-* tokens (opacity and colour-mix only, no fixed colours), plus three starter assets: run-indicator/pulse (default), flash and glow. Regenerate the fixtures and pass check-skin-coverage.

Add the run-indicator and row-state styles to framework/ui/axf.css: running rows get the keyframe pulse, flash or glow and a spinning icon, broke rows get a red/pink background and stop animating, and prefers-reduced-motion is respected. Tokens only.

Add a framework React piece, <RunIndicator> plus a useRowRunState(buildId) hook, that DataGrid rows use through a row-state prop (data-axf-run=running|stale|broke). Register its control@1 targets at the end of the list.

Server side: publish a build-live@1 event on the console live channel for every builds store write (status, step, note, branch, PR) by hooking the store-change path. The UI then needs no polling and no refresh.

VPS liveness tick: a 15-second loop that checks every running build (session, pid, heartbeat) by reading the #772 recovery and #780 stale-row watchdog state instead of re-checking. Push a liveness event only when the state changes, plus a heartbeat summary.
Run the liveness tick: add a cron or systemd timer entry next to axf-pipeline (15 s, under the agent-slots rules, light) and a health@1 check that goes red when the tick stops.

Web client: a live builds store (framework/react or console src) that subscribes to build-live@1 on the live channel, applies events through the engine and reconnects with a resync on reconnect or focus.
Wire the Active, Queue and Pending grids to the live store: rows update in place and running rows get the row-state and RunIndicator.
Wire Incomplete, Build manager, Pipeline and every other grid that lists builds (search for build-row grids) to the live store and row-state.
Broke alert: when a build goes running → broke, send one alert through the alert hub (declared in the plugin's notify.json) and show a pop-up toast in the console that says it broke.

Broke dialog: a framework Dialog (dialog asset) showing the cause, exit code, last step, what the watchdog is doing (from #772 and #780) and a link to the build. It opens from the toast and from the broke row.

Settings: a Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator → Live status sub-tab, with the level toolbar, for the run-indicator asset pick, the animation type, the colour token picks, speed, alerts on/off and the dialog on/off. Values are saved as per-key settings and asset token overrides.
UI Review: build three run-indicator options (pulse, flash, glow) as real assets in plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/run-indicator/ with a choices JSON for the submit step.
REST API: GET /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/live (state of all running builds, liveness, last tick), GET/PUT live/settings, GET live/broke/<id> (dialog data), POST live/broke/<id>/ack.

MCP + CLI: plugin commands for live-status, live-settings get/set and broke-show/ack (MCP through plugin-commands), plus `axf builds live|live-settings|broke <id>`. Add a console-control address for the settings tab, the broke dialog (dialog:build-broke/<id>) and grid rows so console_show and console_open can deep link them.

Voice: AmberX console actions builds.live.status, builds.live.animation (set type, colour, speed) and builds.broke.show, so they match the REST, MCP and CLI parts, and register them with console-control.

Tests: engine fixture checks, a Python test for the liveness tick (alive → stale → broke, no duplicate alerts, reads the watchdog state), a route test, and a client test that an event updates a row without a refresh.

Run CI checks: check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, check-skin-coverage, glossary catalog --check, tracker --check and plugin-lifecycle check. Re-bake the console src/axf and fix what fails.

Take desktop and phone shots of a running row, a broke row, the dialog and the settings tab, and submit them to UI Review with the 3 choices. Then write the report _claude/builds/reports/live-build-status-real-time-grids-15.md (API reach for each feature, watchdog coordination), add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR, saying in it how each feature is reached and that it waits in UI Review.

after.title: Guided live demo test: watch the orchestrator do everything in real time, with an overlay, focus and Next/Pause
after.detail: A guided live demo test of the orchestrator that Brett watches in real time, run on throwaway test builds (never real ones). Before it starts, an overlay with Continue and Pause buttons and a 'Pause between steps' switch. The test walks through everything the orchestrator can do, one thing at a time: queue, launch, steps ticking off/crossed out as they finish, running animation, a deliberate crash, the watchdog catching it, retry, red CI, auto-fix, merge-main, landing, a build dying and showing what failed (red row + alert dialog), stale-row cleanup, phone notifications. For each one: bring the console to focus on the exact grid/row/dialog to watch (console_open / focus), show a caption of what is about to happen, run it live, then wait. With pause on, wait until Brett clicks Next, then wait at least 30 seconds before the next one; with pause off, at least 30 seconds between each. A summary at the end of what passed/failed. Deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice to start/pause/next/stop it. Depends on the live build status build (real-time grids, animated rows, break alerts).

after.title: Auto-lander settings: Log placeholder for the future Log plugin
after.detail: In the auto-lander's settings (Gate plugin, AutoLanderSettings), add a 'Log' section placeholder: an empty slot/registry hook that a future Log plugin fills with the auto-lander's full log (every tick, decision, merge-main, fix attempt, land, error). For now it shows 'Log viewer coming with the Log plugin' plus a link to the existing Attempts list. Make the slot generic so the Log plugin can attach to any plugin's settings the same way.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 9 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I need a log for the auto-lander that I can view from its settings. We're gonna build a log plugin later, so just put a placeholder for it.

steps.text: Design the generic settings-slot contract (settings-slot@1): a slot id like 'log', a host key (plugin id plus settings section), what a provider registers (render component, label, priority), and what shows when nobody fills it (placeholder text plus fallback links). Write it to framework/spec/SETTINGS-SLOTS.md so any plugin's settings can host a slot and a future Log plugin can fill one for any host.
Add the settings-slot registry core: register, unregister, list for a host, and resolve to the provider or the placeholder. Keep it pure, with no React. Add a fixture and a check script.

Add the React SettingsSlot component. It reads the registry and renders the provider when one is registered, otherwise the placeholder with its fallback links. Use framework controls and tokens only, plus a data-axf-target address. Export it from framework/react and re-bake it into the console's src/axf.

Add a 'Log' section to the Gate plugin's AutoLanderSettings using <SettingsSlot host="gate.auto-lander" slot="log">. The placeholder reads 'Log viewer coming with the Log plugin' and links to the existing Attempts list. List what the future log will hold (every tick, decision, merge-main, fix attempt, land, error) as the slot's declared contents.

Add the API side. Give the Log section and the Attempts link control@1 / console-control addresses (deep link view:settings/tab:plugins/gate/auto-lander#log) so console_show and console_open open them. Add a REST route GET /api/plugins/gate/settings-slots that returns which slots exist and whether each is filled.

Reach the slot state through every API surface: an MCP plugin command (gate_settings_slots), the CLI (axf gate slots [--host]) and a voice action (settings.slots), all returning the same thing as REST. Add descriptions so the glossary picks them up.

Add a register API for future providers: a capability service axf.settings-slots@1 (register/list) so the Log plugin can attach to any plugin's settings without naming folders. Add lifecycle markers, and document it in the Gate plugin README.

Prepare the UI Review submission: 3 placeholder options (inline note, collapsed card, empty-state panel), each as an asset under apps/console-web/plugins/gate/assets/, with desktop and phone shots. Submit them with review.mjs --choices.

The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.

- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- The axHub badge is red unless settings come live from axHub (Oct 24 2026, Brett): any axHub status badge or indicator starts red and turns green only while the app is reading its settings live from axHub right now (a fresh read of the hub's settings document succeeded, and a developer app's own hub source is ready). Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. - Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Every banner launches expanded (activity, build manager, codebase changes, approvals, systems check, keys, What's new). Activity still only appears while something runs or just finished.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. steps.text: Plan the skin in Plan Studio first: add a plan for 'Flagship professional skin' with Brett's verbatim words. Inventory every surface it must cover (colours, style, layout, context/app/nav menus, tab groups, toolbars, banners and widgets, grids, dialogs, settings interfaces, animations, behaviour, hooks) and every app it must reach (console, axHub web, AmberX). Commit the plan JSON.

Audit skin@1 against the registry. Run skin-coverage over asset-types.json and list each surface from step 1 as covered (slot / parts / reference / bundle) or not expressible yet (expected gaps: motion/animation, behaviour, hooks, grid density, dialog chrome, settings-interface layout). Write the gap table into the report draft.

Design the new skin@1 slots for the gaps: motion (durations, easings, enter/exit per chrome kind, reduced-motion), behaviour (tap-confirm arm time, hover/press feedback, overflow modes, sticky/collapse defaults), hooks (hook@1 / drop-target@1 refs per chrome kind), grid (row density, rows per item, header style) and dialog/settings chrome. Write them into the skin@1 entry in asset-types.json as optional, additive slots so old skins stay valid.
Regenerate the JSON Schemas and update the skin validators (TS reference and mjs) for the new slots. The validators must accept old skins unchanged and reject bad values for the new slots.

Teach the skin engine the motion and behaviour slots: compile motion into --fx-motion-* tokens and behaviour into settings-layer defaults (tapconfirm armMs, overflow, sticky). Precedence stays child-overrides-parent through resolveLookSkin. Unset slots compile to today's defaults.

Teach the skin engine the hooks, grid and dialog/settings slots: hook refs per chrome kind are resolved through hook@1, grid density/rows feed the DataGrid tokens, and dialog/settings chrome picks the settings asset per kind (chrome-settings@1).

A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

steps.text: Reproduce and find the cause: trace how the console restores its place on load (view/route state in apps/console-web/src, URL hash/query, sessionStorage/localStorage keys, console.refresh handler, service worker/hot reload, pull-to-refresh). Write findings (which state is lost: view, tab, scroll, selection; and the scroll-lock cause after an update) to _claude/builds/reports/fix-refreshing-console-jumps-back.md as a draft

Check the scroll lock after an update: find what leaves body/root overflow hidden or a scrim/pointer-events overlay after an update or refresh banner (update toast, dialog close, pull-to-refresh handler, overscroll-behavior) and note the exact file:line in the draft report

Add a console place store: one small module (apps/console-web/src/place/placeState.ts) that saves the current view address, active tab per tab group, selection and scroll offsets of the main scroller and named panes to sessionStorage (debounced, on pagehide/visibilitychange too), keyed by console-control addresses (view:/tab:/row:)

Restore view + tab on load: wire the place store into the console's router/app shell so a reload reopens the saved view and tabs before the first paint, and URL deep links still win over the saved place

Restore scroll + selection: after the restored view mounts and its data loads, reapply scroll offsets (retry until content is tall enough, give up after a short timeout) and the selected row/item; stop any default scroll-to-top or default-tab reset that fires after load
Server-pushed console.refresh keeps the place: make the refresh handler (soft and --hard) save the place right before reloading and the soft refresh re-render without resetting view/tab/scroll
Pull-down refresh keeps the place: make the pull-to-refresh path save and restore the same state as reload, and leave scroll unlocked when it finishes
Fix the scroll lock after an update: clear any leftover overflow/pointer-events lock or stale overlay when the update/refresh flow ends (and on load as a safety net), using the cause found in step 2

API part: expose the saved place read-only and the restore action through the console API, keeping all four drivers the same: REST GET/POST /api/console-control place (read state, restore), MCP console tool, axf console place [get|restore], and an AmberX voice action; register targets with control@1 (append-only)

Tests: a unit test for placeState save/restore/deep-link precedence and a Playwright check against vite preview: open a tab deep in a view, scroll, select a row, reload, pull-refresh and server-push refresh; assert the same place is restored and the page still scrolls

Run the checks (typecheck, check-theme, check-controls, check-console-control, check-toolbars), finish the report _claude/builds/reports/fix-refreshing-console-jumps-back.md (cause, fix, before/after), update the THREADS row and open the PR naming how each part is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice)

after.title: Dispatcher: split builds evenly across Claude accounts
after.detail: Bug: the orchestrator plans every build on hulu0241 (5/5 full) while mossesx-max- (Moses X) sits at 0/5. Fix the dispatcher/planner in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/pipeline.mjs (planned.account, loadOwnAccounts, accounts.json) so subscription accounts are filled round-robin: alternate accounts per launch and always pick the account with the fewest running builds, keeping running counts equal (e.g. 3/3, not 5/0). Re-plan already-planned Pending/Queue builds when they launch, not stick to the stale planned account. API keys stay off until both subscriptions are busy. Show per-account running counts in the pipeline status. Add a test. Land as soon as green.

notes.text: Brett: run this now on Fable, on the hulu0241 account. Top priority.

Brett: also, when a build comes in with a chosen model and/or account (pinned by Brett in a note, the console, MCP, CLI or voice), the dispatcher must use exactly that model and account, never override it. Even split applies only to builds with no account chosen. Make model + account settable fields on a build through every API.
Queued by console.

Brett: the only real cap is the VPS total of 8 builds at once (agent-slots maxBuilds 8). Per-account building/queue limits: 0 means no limit. Set both subscription accounts (hulu0241, mossesx-max-) to 0 in claude-accounts workers.json so they're unlimited, and the total 8 is split evenly between them (4 and 4).
Split by Claude into 13 steps (0 Fable).

Brett: ONE setting only. Moses X was 'take jobs' ON in Claude accounts but 'use' OFF in the orchestrator's own pipeline accounts.json, so it never got builds. Remove the duplicate: the orchestrator reads account on/off, limits and roles only from the Claude accounts plugin (workers.json). Delete the pipeline's own use/parallel per-account record (migrate it), and remove that control from the orchestrator UI/API. One place, one switch.

origin.said: We need it to split evenly. One and one and one and one. Every other one. The same amount running on each account.

steps.text: Read apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/pipeline.mjs (tick, planned.account, loadOwnAccounts, accounts.json reading, account routing) and deploy/claude-workers.mjs route; write down in the build notes where an account gets picked and stuck to a build

Add a pure helper pickAccount(accounts, running, lastPicked, model) in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/account-balance.mjs: subscription accounts only, those able to run the phase's model, fewest running builds first, tie broken by round-robin after the last account picked; API-key accounts only when every subscription account is at its cap

Add runningByAccount(): count running builds per account from live sessions/agent slots (not from planned.account), plus a persisted lastPicked cursor in the plugin's data dir through data-store@1 (data-files.mjs)
Wire pickAccount into pipeline.mjs tick: choose the account at launch time, pass it to deploy/claude-headless.sh --account, update the cursor; ignore any stale planned.account on Pending/Queue builds

Make loadOwnAccounts / accounts.json reading mark each account subscription vs API key and its per-account cap; API keys stay off until both subscriptions are busy (at cap)
Add per-account running counts (running/cap, e.g. 3/5 · 3/5) to `pipeline.mjs status` output and its JSON (accounts: [{id,label,running,cap,kind}])
Expose the same counts through the plugin's REST status route and MCP (plugin-commands) so console API, MCP, CLI and voice read one shape
Show per-account running counts in the Pipeline tab status strip (framework Chip/TabGroup controls, tokens only), registering a data-axf-target for console_show deep link

origin.brief:
# Build: move-everything-axhub-web-console

## Brett said (verbatim)
> I really need to get this axHub and AmberX over the console. I really need that done. With the phone app.

## What to build
Continue build "Move everything from axHub web into the console" (move-everything-axhub-web-console) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"I really need to get this axHub and AmberX over the console. I really need that done. With the phone app."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (155 left, ~23 h):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Inventory every axHub web page, option and setting (approvals, approval log, passes, veto/countdown, users, account, apps/connectors, services, handoff, auth admin, each settings page) and the axHub REST/MCP endpoint behind each one; write the parity map as a hub-console@1 spec draft and save the whole migration as a parked Plan Studio plan
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Define the hub-console@1 contract: one console address per hub screen (view:hub/…), the state shape each screen reads, the action list per screen with personOnly flags (approve/deny/shelve/grant pass stay person-only), and how the console reads them through the hub (proxy, own session, never the console token for decisions); add the schema and a fixture
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Write the hub-console@1 validator and route table (framework/core/hub-console.mjs) with a spec check that holds it to the fixture, and record the deferred Android twin in PORTING.md
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Design the migration of axHub web's saved UI settings (per-user page prefs, approval view options, connector display options) into console settings keys, and write the one-shot migration script with a dry-run mode
[ ] s5 (~8 min) Scaffold the hub-admin console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith, lifecycle dataDir, settings tab under Plugins), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, and an empty Hub view group registered on the console nav
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Server side of the plugin: a FastAPI router that proxies the hub-console@1 reads to axHub with retries and a clear unavailable state, plus its unit tests
[ ] s7 (~10 min) Approvals screen: live list of held/confirm calls with countdown, title-first reason, collapsible code, and Approve / Deny / Shelve through the approvals-banner relay (Brett's own hub session, personOnly), on framework controls and the tab-group asset
[ ] s8 (~8 min) Approvals API part: deep link view:hub/tab:approvals, state read REST + MCP tool hub_approvals_list, CLI `axf hub approvals`, voice action hub.approvals; decide actions registered personOnly so no session can run them
[ ] s9 (~8 min) Approval log screen: searchable history of decided/expired/denied calls with filters (service, tool, who, outcome) as a DataGrid
[ ] s10 (~6 min) Approval log API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_approval_log, CLI `axf hub approval-log`, voice hub.approvalLog
[ ] s11 (~10 min) Passes and veto settings screen: active passes with revoke, grant pass form (service, tools/scope, minutes), veto countdown length and No-wait status shown read-only where owner-only
[ ] s12 (~8 min) Passes/veto API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_passes_list / hub_pass_revoke / hub_pass_request (grant stays Brett's click), CLI `axf hub passes`, voice hub.passes; countdown setting through control@1
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Users screen: list, invite, roles, disable, with destructive actions behind confirm
[ ] s14 (~8 min) Users API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_users_*, CLI `axf hub users`, voice hub.users; role changes and disable need confirm
[ ] s15 (~8 min) Account screen: profile, sessions/devices with sign-out, linked phone, notification prefs
[ ] s16 (~6 min) Account API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_account_*, CLI `axf hub account`, voice hub.account
[ ] s17 (~10 min) Apps/connectors screen: connected services with status, policies per tool (allow/veto/confirm), add/reconnect/remove connector, token health shown as systems-check items
[ ] s18 (~10 min) Services detail screen: one service's tools, schemas, policy editor and recent calls
[ ] s19 (~10 min) Connectors/services API: deep links (view:hub/tab:connectors, row:<service>), REST + MCP hub_services_list / hub_service_get / hub_policy_set / hub_connector_remove (confirm), CLI `axf hub services`, voice hub.services; register a health@1 check for dead connector keys
[ ] s20 (~8 min) Handoff screen: open handoffs between devices/sessions, send, accept, clear
[ ] s21 (~6 min) Handoff API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_handoff_*, CLI `axf hub handoff`, voice hub.handoff
[ ] s22 (~10 min) Auth admin screen: OAuth clients, API tokens (create shows once, revoke with confirm), sign-in methods; no secret ever stored in the console
[ ] s23 (~8 min) Auth admin API: deep link, REST + MCP hub_auth_*, CLI `axf hub auth`, voice hub.auth; token create/revoke personOnly or confirm per the contract
[ ] s24 (~10 min) Hub settings: one Settings → Plugins → Hub sub-tab with the level toolbar, every former axHub web setting as a registered setting; run the settings migration from step 4 against a copy and wire it into install.mjs
[ ] s25 (~10 min) Console-control registration: every hub screen, tab, row and action gets its control address (data-axf-target), toolbars role=toolbar + settings ids, tab rows through TabGroup; make check-console-control, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-theme and check-controls pass
[ ] s26 (~8 min) Phone Connect tie-in: hub approval and veto notices open the console's Approvals screen through Phone Connect deep links instead of the AmberX app; note the overlap with builds phone-connect and remove-amberx-app-code-once-phone on those builds
[ ] s27 (~8 min) Parity check: a script that walks the hub-console@1 route table and fails when any axHub web page/action has no console screen, deep link, REST route, MCP tool, CLI command or voice action; add it to CI
[ ] s28 (~10 min) Retire the axHub web UI from this repo's side: apps/axhub-web marked retired in its manifest, axhub.amberxai.com UI paths redirect to the console's Hub screens (deploy config), shared-assets list updated; open the matching axHub-repo change as a follow-up item (server stays backend/MCP only)
[ ] s29 (~8 min) Docs and help: plugin README, help entries, glossary descriptions, decision line in memory/decisions.md, rule line that the console is the only hub UI

after.title: Auto-lander: never wait on a missing UI Review, and test the real lander
after.detail: Bug: PR #816 (guided-live-demo-test-watch-orchestrator) was finished, CI green, but never merged on its own: the auto-lander held it for a UI Review pick whose review item was never posted to the console, so it would wait forever. Brett had to land it by hand. Fix: 1) The lander never holds a PR for a UI Review item that doesn't exist in the console; a missing or unposted review never blocks landing (land when CI is green, flag the review separately). 2) Any held PR older than a set time shows in the systems check banner with the reason and a Land now button. 3) Builds that ship UI Review items must post them to the live console (fail the build step if they can't). 4) The orchestrator demo must run its landing act against the real lander path (self-test before demo), not only a dry run. Tests. Land when green.

notes.text: Brett: UI Review must NEVER block landing at all, posted or not. Auto-landing means no human step: land as soon as CI is green; UI Review picks happen after, as a follow-up that swaps the chosen asset in. Remove the UI Review hold from the lander entirely.
Queued by console.
Split by Claude into 17 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: If it recorded the test of the pipeline and didn't merge it on its own, then the test failed. It should have tested itself before it did the demo.

steps.text: gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.

lander-state@1 schema: add heldSince, holdReason and reviewFlag (missing|unposted|waiting) to each PR record. Migration: existing held records get heldSince = their last-seen time. Regenerate the fixture with check-gate-rules.mjs --write.
Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.

Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.
Merge queue / landing line: use the new verdict, so a stack entry whose review is missing goes ahead and is not parked. Write heldSince and holdReason to lander-state when an entry is truly held.

Flagged reviews: when a PR lands with a missing or unposted review, file a UI Review notice (Screenshots group '<build id> - missing review') and add a build note, so the review is flagged separately and nothing blocks.

Gate plugin setting 'Held PR alert after' (minutes, default 60) in Settings → Plugins → Gate, saved through the gate settings store. Add the API: REST setting route, MCP plugin command, `axf gate settings set heldAlertMin`, and a voice action.

Systems check health@1 check 'held-prs': lists every lander-held PR older than the setting, with the PR, its build, the reason and how long it has been held. It turns red past the limit and is pushed once to the AmberX app.

'Land now' fix on the held-prs banner item: puts the PR into the merge queue at the front with an override note (never a direct merge). It is a destructive press, so it needs confirm. API: REST POST /api/plugins/gate/land-now, an MCP command, `axf gate land-now <pr>`, a voice action, and a console_show deep link to the item (row:held-prs/pr:<n>).
Register the banner item and the Land now button as console-control targets (data-axf-target). Add the state read (GET held PRs with reasons). Pass check-console-control.mjs.

Builds that ship UI Review items must post them to the live console. review.mjs submit --console exits non-zero when the console doesn't confirm the item id, and the build step that submits fails instead of carrying on.

Build rule 'ui-review-posted' in the build-rules store: when a build records UI Review choices, the VPS checks that each item exists in the console before the step is ticked, and otherwise marks the step failed with the reason.

Orchestrator demo self-test: before the demo runs its landing act, run the real lander path on a throwaway PR state through the real gate verdict, the real review lookup and the queue add in check mode. If the self-test fails, the demo stops and files a systems check item instead of recording.

Demo landing act runs for real (not only a dry run): it confirms the demo PR reaches the merge queue and merges. If it doesn't merge, the demo is marked failed. Add the API: REST demo self-test route, an MCP command, `axf demo selftest`, and a voice action.

Regression test that replays PR #816: CI green, review item absent from the console → the lander lands it. Also: held > limit → the held-prs check is red with Land now; a submit that can't post → the step fails.
Help and docs: gate plugin README, ui-review README (must post, fails otherwise), systems-check README (held-prs) and the decisions.md line, with the API paths for each feature.

gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.

Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.

Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.
Merge queue / landing line: use the new verdict, so a stack entry whose review is missing goes ahead and is not parked. Write heldSince and holdReason to lander-state when an entry is truly held.

Flagged reviews: when a PR lands with a missing or unposted review, file a UI Review notice (Screenshots group '<build id> - missing review') and add a build note, so the review is flagged separately and nothing blocks.

Gate plugin setting 'Held PR alert after' (minutes, default 60) in Settings → Plugins → Gate, saved through the gate settings store. Add the API: REST setting route, MCP plugin command, `axf gate settings set heldAlertMin`, and a voice action.

Systems check health@1 check 'held-prs': lists every lander-held PR older than the setting, with the PR, its build, the reason and how long it has been held. It turns red past the limit and is pushed once to the AmberX app.

'Land now' fix on the held-prs banner item: puts the PR into the merge queue at the front with an override note (never a direct merge). It is a destructive press, so it needs confirm. API: REST POST /api/plugins/gate/land-now, an MCP command, `axf gate land-now <pr>`, a voice action, and a console_show deep link to the item (row:held-prs/pr:<n>).
Register the banner item and the Land now button as console-control targets (data-axf-target). Add the state read (GET held PRs with reasons). Pass check-console-control.mjs.

Builds that ship UI Review items must post them to the live console. review.mjs submit --console exits non-zero when the console doesn't confirm the item id, and the build step that submits fails instead of carrying on.

Build rule 'ui-review-posted' in the build-rules store: when a build records UI Review choices, the VPS checks that each item exists in the console before the step is ticked, and otherwise marks the step failed with the reason.

Orchestrator demo self-test: before the demo runs its landing act, run the real lander path on a throwaway PR state through the real gate verdict, the real review lookup and the queue add in check mode. If the self-test fails, the demo stops and files a systems check item instead of recording.

Demo landing act runs for real (not only a dry run): it confirms the demo PR reaches the merge queue and merges. If it doesn't merge, the demo is marked failed. Add the API: REST demo self-test route, an MCP command, `axf demo selftest`, and a voice action.

Regression test that replays PR #816: CI green, review item absent from the console → the lander lands it. Also: held > limit → the held-prs check is red with Land now; a submit that can't post → the step fails.
Help and docs: gate plugin README, ui-review README (must post, fails otherwise), systems-check README (held-prs) and the decisions.md line, with the API paths for each feature.

Run the checks: check-gate-rules, check-landing-line, check-console-control, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, and the plugin tests. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-lander-never-wait-missing-ui-review.md (before/after, the #816 replay, and how each feature is reached by REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Add the THREADS row, open the PR and add it to the merge queue so it lands when green.

gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.

lander-state@1 schema: add heldSince, holdReason and reviewFlag (missing|unposted|waiting) to each PR record. Migration: existing held records get heldSince = their last-seen time. Regenerate the fixture with check-gate-rules.mjs --write.
Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.

Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.
Merge queue / landing line: use the new verdict, so a stack entry whose review is missing goes ahead and is not parked. Write heldSince and holdReason to lander-state when an entry is truly held.

Flagged reviews: when a PR lands with a missing or unposted review, file a UI Review notice (Screenshots group '<build id> - missing review') and add a build note, so the review is flagged separately and nothing blocks.

Gate plugin setting 'Held PR alert after' (minutes, default 60) in Settings → Plugins → Gate, saved through the gate settings store. Add the API: REST setting route, MCP plugin command, `axf gate settings set heldAlertMin`, and a voice action.

Systems check health@1 check 'held-prs': lists every lander-held PR older than the setting, with the PR, its build, the reason and how long it has been held. It turns red past the limit and is pushed once to the AmberX app.

'Land now' fix on the held-prs banner item: puts the PR into the merge queue at the front with an override note (never a direct merge). It is a destructive press, so it needs confirm. API: REST POST /api/plugins/gate/land-now, an MCP command, `axf gate land-now <pr>`, a voice action, and a console_show deep link to the item (row:held-prs/pr:<n>).

Builds that ship UI Review items must post them to the live console. review.mjs submit --console exits non-zero when the console doesn't confirm the item id, and the build step that submits fails instead of carrying on.

Build rule 'ui-review-posted' in the build-rules store: when a build records UI Review choices, the VPS checks that each item exists in the console before the step is ticked, and otherwise marks the step failed with the reason.

gate-rules@1 verdict contract: a UI Review hold applies only when the review item exists in the console. A missing or unposted review gives the verdict 'land, review flagged' (new verdict reason ui-review-missing) instead of 'hold'. Update the spec and the default rule set.

lander-state@1 schema: add heldSince, holdReason and reviewFlag (missing|unposted|waiting) to each PR record. Migration: existing held records get heldSince = their last-seen time. Regenerate the fixture with check-gate-rules.mjs --write.
Add check-gate-rules cases: review item missing → land; review unposted → land with a flag; review waiting or changes asked → hold; review rejected → hold; the held-age field is filled in.

Lander: before holding a PR on UI Review, look the item up in the live console (review.mjs state --pr N --console / GET ui-review state). Not found → land when CI is green and record reviewFlag. Never treat a failed lookup as a hold.

after.title: One true source for every setting
after.detail: Rule from Brett: every setting has exactly one true source. Audit the console, plugins, orchestrator, axHub and framework for any setting stored or editable in more than one place (example found: Claude account on/off lived in both claude-accounts workers.json and the orchestrator's pipeline accounts.json, so Moses X looked on but never got builds). For each duplicate: pick the one source, migrate values, make every other place read from it (no copies), remove duplicate controls/APIs. Add a CI check that fails when a setting key is defined or written in two stores. Write the rule into the shared build rules so every future build follows it. Report listing each duplicate found and fixed.

notes.text: Queued by console.
Split by Claude into 20 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: All settings need one true fucking source.

steps.text: Design the settings-source@1 contract: a registry file framework/schemas/settings-sources.json mapping every setting key (or key prefix) to exactly one owning store (data-store namespace + path + owner plugin/module), with readers/writers lists and a 'mirrors' field that must be empty; write the spec framework/spec/SETTINGS-SOURCES.md (one owner per key, readers resolve through the owner, no copies, how a migration moves a key from one store to another)

Write the resolver core framework/core/settings-source.mjs: load the registry, ownerOf(key), readSetting(key) / writeSetting(key, value) routed through data-files.mjs to the owning store only, refuse writes to a non-owner path; plus a fixture framework/spec/fixtures/settings-sources.json with golden owner lookups (exact keys, prefixes, unknown keys)

Design the migration helper framework/cli/settings-migrate.mjs: for a duplicated key, read every store that holds it, pick the owner's value (newest-wins when the owner is unset, recorded), write it to the owner, strip the key from the other stores, journal before/after in _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/migrations.json; --dry-run lists what would move

Audit pass 1, console server + plugins: scan apps/console-web/server and apps/console-web/plugins/*/ for settings files and keys (settings.json, *.json under dataDir, SettingsRegistry keys, data_store writes); write the raw inventory to _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/audit-console.json (key, store, file, writer, editor UI)

Audit pass 2, orchestrator + pipeline + agent stores: build-orchestrator (pipeline accounts.json, orchestrator settings), claude-accounts (workers.json), agent-slots, claude-settings, gate/lander settings, push-banner settings; add to the inventory as audit-builds.json

Audit pass 3, framework + axHub side: framework/core settings (SettingsRegistry keys, appearance@1 / app-look@1 / skins, tapconfirm, chrome settings), framework/libs/settings, lib-hub, axhub-adapter-axf plugin and hub settings documents under /projects/_shared/_data; add audit-framework.json

Collate the three inventories into the duplicate list: every key held or editable in more than one store or with more than one editing UI/API; for each pick the true owner with a one-line reason; write duplicates.md and fill framework/schemas/settings-sources.json with every audited key and its owner

Fix duplicate 1, Claude account on/off: make claude-accounts workers.json the one owner of account enabled/worker state; build-orchestrator pipeline reads it through settings-source.mjs (no accounts.json copy of on/off); run settings-migrate for those keys so Moses X's real state is kept

Remove the duplicate account on/off control and API from the orchestrator (pipeline accounts UI toggle, its REST route and MCP command) and point them at the claude-accounts ones (deep link view:builds/tab:claude-accounts, same REST/MCP/CLI/voice action); update plugin-commands routes and console-control targets

Fix the next duplicates from duplicates.md in the build stores (e.g. agent caps, lander/auto-merge switches, model defaults between claude-settings and orchestrator): one owner each, readers through settings-source.mjs, migrate values, delete the copies

Remove the duplicate controls/APIs for the build-store duplicates just fixed: the non-owner settings fields become a read-only line with a 'Change in <owner>' link (console_show deep link); drop their write routes and MCP/CLI/voice aliases, keeping one action per setting

Fix the console server + plugin duplicates from duplicates.md (settings kept both in a plugin dataDir and the console settings registry or local storage): one owner, migrate, readers resolve through server/data_store.py owner lookup

Python twin of the resolver: server/settings_source.py reads framework/schemas/settings-sources.json and refuses a write to a non-owner path; wire data_store.py writes through it; unit test in server tests

Fix the framework/axHub duplicates from duplicates.md (e.g. look values held in both appearance@1 and app-look@1 or local SettingsRegistry copies, hub vs repo settings snapshots): one owner, migrate, remove local copies; record any Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md

Run settings-migrate.mjs for every remaining duplicate on the real hub data (dry-run first, then apply), commit the migration journal, verify each owner holds the expected value and the old stores no longer carry the key

API for the registry: REST GET /api/settings-sources (list, owner of key, duplicates found by a live scan), MCP console tools settings_source_owner / settings_source_check, CLI `axf settings-source owner|list|check`, voice action settings.source, deep link view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=sources

Small read-only Settings → Sources view listing each setting key, its one owner and a jump to the owner's control (framework DataGrid + TabGroup, tokens only, data-axf-target registered); submit 3 UI Review options per the ui-choices rule

Write the resolver core framework/core/settings-source.mjs: load the registry, ownerOf(key), readSetting(key) / writeSetting(key, value) routed through data-files.mjs to the owning store only, refuse writes to a non-owner path; plus a fixture framework/spec/fixtures/settings-sources.json with golden owner lookups (exact keys, prefixes, unknown keys)

Design the migration helper framework/cli/settings-migrate.mjs: for a duplicated key, read every store that holds it, pick the owner's value (newest-wins when the owner is unset, recorded), write it to the owner, strip the key from the other stores, journal before/after in _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/migrations.json; --dry-run lists what would move

Audit pass 1, console server + plugins: scan apps/console-web/server and apps/console-web/plugins/*/ for settings files and keys (settings.json, *.json under dataDir, SettingsRegistry keys, data_store writes); write the raw inventory to _claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/audit-console.json (key, store, file, writer, editor UI)

Audit pass 2, orchestrator + pipeline + agent stores: build-orchestrator (pipeline accounts.json, orchestrator settings), claude-accounts (workers.json), agent-slots, claude-settings, gate/lander settings, push-banner settings; add to the inventory as audit-builds.json

Audit pass 3, framework + axHub side: framework/core settings (SettingsRegistry keys, appearance@1 / app-look@1 / skins, tapconfirm, chrome settings), framework/libs/settings, lib-hub, axhub-adapter-axf plugin and hub settings documents under /projects/_shared/_data; add audit-framework.json

Collate the three inventories into the duplicate list: every key held or editable in more than one store or with more than one editing UI/API; for each pick the true owner with a one-line reason; write duplicates.md and fill framework/schemas/settings-sources.json with every audited key and its owner

Fix duplicate 1, Claude account on/off: make claude-accounts workers.json the one owner of account enabled/worker state; build-orchestrator pipeline reads it through settings-source.mjs (no accounts.json copy of on/off); run settings-migrate for those keys so Moses X's real state is kept

Remove the duplicate account on/off control and API from the orchestrator (pipeline accounts UI toggle, its REST route and MCP command) and point them at the claude-accounts ones (deep link view:builds/tab:claude-accounts, same REST/MCP/CLI/voice action); update plugin-commands routes and console-control targets

Fix the next duplicates from duplicates.md in the build stores (e.g. agent caps, lander/auto-merge switches, model defaults between claude-settings and orchestrator): one owner each, readers through settings-source.mjs, migrate values, delete the copies

Remove the duplicate controls/APIs for the build-store duplicates just fixed: the non-owner settings fields become a read-only line with a 'Change in <owner>' link (console_show deep link); drop their write routes and MCP/CLI/voice aliases, keeping one action per setting

Fix the console server + plugin duplicates from duplicates.md (settings kept both in a plugin dataDir and the console settings registry or local storage): one owner, migrate, readers resolve through server/data_store.py owner lookup

Python twin of the resolver: server/settings_source.py reads framework/schemas/settings-sources.json and refuses a write to a non-owner path; wire data_store.py writes through it; unit test in server tests

Fix the framework/axHub duplicates from duplicates.md (e.g. look values held in both appearance@1 and app-look@1 or local SettingsRegistry copies, hub vs repo settings snapshots): one owner, migrate, remove local copies; record any Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md

Run settings-migrate.mjs for every remaining duplicate on the real hub data (dry-run first, then apply), commit the migration journal, verify each owner holds the expected value and the old stores no longer carry the key

after.title: VPS sets every build status in the manifest; orchestrator files tabs from it
after.detail: Rule from Brett: the VPS is the only thing that sets a build's status. Status lives in the build manifest the VPS owns. As soon as a build starts on the VPS, its manifest status becomes building. When the VPS hands a build back to the orchestrator (stopped, killed, crashed, paused, kicked out) and its status is building or on hold, the orchestrator files it straight into the Hold tab: never Pending, never auto-relaunched. The orchestrator never computes status itself; it only reads the manifest status and puts the build in the matching tab. Hold must work on running builds too (stop the session on the VPS, keep the branch and ticked steps, file to Hold). Today hold only works on queued builds, and a paused build (flagship-professional-skin-covering-2) got relaunched on its own. Add tests: started build returned => Hold; held build never relaunched by the dispatcher. Part of the everything-on-the-VPS rule; coordinate with move-server-side-console-parts-onto-vps.

notes.text: Queued by console.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (3 Fable).

Brett: Pending is ONLY for builds that have never started. Once a build has started, it never goes back to Pending. Today the orchestrator sends stopped, needs-brett, upgrade-blocked and crash-limit builds back to Pending (README session-end table); change all of those. A started build that comes back as building goes to the Queue, one that comes back as on hold goes to Hold, a failed one goes to Errors. Move every already-started build now sitting in Pending (steps done > 0 or runs > 0) to the right tab during migration.

origin.said: All the status updates are going to be filed by the VPS. Attached to the manifest, and when it's sent back to the orchestrator, he knows what tab to put it in. If it gets kicked out of the VPS and sent back to the orchestrator as building at any time, whether it's building or on hold, it's going to go into hold.

steps.text: Design build-manifest status contract: add VPS-owned `status` (building|on-hold|stopped|done|…) with `setBy:'vps'`, `setAt`, `reason` (stopped/killed/crashed/paused/kicked-out) to the build manifest schema in framework/schemas and the builds@1 record; document in framework/spec/BUILD-STATUS.md (VPS is sole writer, orchestrator read-only)

Write the status→tab mapping core: pure function fileTab(manifest) in framework/core/build-status-tabs.mjs (building or on-hold when returned => hold; never pending; queued => queue; done => built/complete) plus migration note for existing store records without manifest status
Migration: builds-store.mjs reads legacy status as manifest status once (setBy:'migration'), journalled; verify keeps every build; add fixture framework/spec/fixtures/build-status-tabs.json
VPS side: deploy/claude-headless.sh sets manifest status=building through a new framework/cli/build-manifest.mjs `set-status <id> building --by vps` the moment a session starts

VPS side: on session exit (stop, kill, crash, pause, kick-out) the launcher trap records the return reason on the manifest and hands it back to the orchestrator via build-manifest.mjs `return <id> --reason …` without changing status

Orchestrator: remove its own status computation in pipeline.mjs / orchestrator.mjs; on return it reads manifest status and files the build with fileTab() (building/on-hold => Hold); never Pending, never requeue

Dispatcher guard: pipeline.mjs tick skips any build whose manifest status is on-hold or filed in Hold, and drops the 'crash → back to Queue, 3 runs' path (fixes the flagship-professional-skin-covering-2 relaunch)

Hold on running builds: build-manifest.mjs `hold <id>` asks the VPS to stop the session (agent-slots / headless pid), keeps branch and ticked steps, VPS sets status=on-hold, orchestrator files to Hold

Console server routes: GET /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/manifest/<id> (status read), POST …/hold and …/release (release moves Hold → Pending only by Brett's call); console_show target for the Hold tab and a build row
Console UI: Pipeline tab shows tab from manifest status, a Hold button on running rows (confirm), a 'set by VPS · reason' line on held rows; register control targets (data-axf-target)
API parity: MCP plugin commands (pipeline-hold, pipeline-release, manifest-status), axf CLI `axf builds hold|release|status`, AmberX voice actions; all calling the same routes
Tests: framework/spec/check-build-status-tabs.mjs (fixture; started build returned => Hold for every reason; on-hold returned => Hold; never Pending); orchestrator refuses to write status itself
Tests: dispatcher test — held build never relaunched over N ticks, running-build hold stops the fake session and keeps branch + ticked steps; wire both checks into CI

VPS side: deploy/claude-headless.sh sets manifest status=building through a new framework/cli/build-manifest.mjs `set-status <id> building --by vps` the moment a session starts

VPS side: on session exit (stop, kill, crash, pause, kick-out) the launcher trap records the return reason on the manifest and hands it back to the orchestrator via build-manifest.mjs `return <id> --reason …` without changing status

Orchestrator: remove its own status computation in pipeline.mjs / orchestrator.mjs; on return it reads manifest status and files the build with fileTab() (building/on-hold => Hold); never Pending, never requeue

Dispatcher guard: pipeline.mjs tick skips any build whose manifest status is on-hold or filed in Hold, and drops the 'crash → back to Queue, 3 runs' path (fixes the flagship-professional-skin-covering-2 relaunch)

Hold on running builds: build-manifest.mjs `hold <id>` asks the VPS to stop the session (agent-slots / headless pid), keeps branch and ticked steps, VPS sets status=on-hold, orchestrator files to Hold

Console UI: Pipeline tab shows tab from manifest status, a Hold button on running rows (confirm), a 'set by VPS · reason' line on held rows; register control targets (data-axf-target)
API parity: MCP plugin commands (pipeline-hold, pipeline-release, manifest-status), axf CLI `axf builds hold|release|status`, AmberX voice actions; all calling the same routes

Tests: dispatcher test — held build never relaunched over N ticks, running-build hold stops the fake session and keeps branch + ticked steps; wire both checks into CI

Run all checks (builds-store verify, check-builds-store, check-build-status-tabs, pipeline tests, console-control, check-theme), write _claude/builds/reports/vps-sets-every-build-status-manifest.md (API reach per feature), THREADS row, UI Review submission, open PR

after.title: Voice drives the whole app: your mouth is the mouse (Fable sweep)
after.detail: Brett: the API must fully control the entire app. Found in a live demo: Plan Studio 2.0 'plan-studio-2.new' and 'new-inside' only open a blank Plan item dialog; the text passed as args never fills Title/Note, and there is no console-control command to set a dialog field (title, note, kind, priority, model, checkbox, any input). Fix at the framework level: every input, textarea, select, switch and checkbox in every console dialog and screen gets a console-control address (field:<dialog>/<name>) with set/get, and a dialog submit/save. Action args that name a value (new:<title>) must fill the form and save. Plan Studio 2.0 first (new, new-inside, rename with text, note, priority, model), then sweep all plugins. CI check: fails on any form control without a settable address. Same through REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Test: create a nested plan with titles, notes and ticked checkboxes entirely through the API and verify it on screen.

notes.text: Queued by console.
On hold (console). It keeps its place in the Queue; the dispatcher skips it until released.
Brett: run this on Fable as a sweep of the WHOLE console, but only after move-everything-axhub-web-console (axHub + AmberX moved into the console) has landed. On hold until then.

Brett, full scope (Fable): the WHOLE app, every single piece, controllable by voice through the API, 'as if your mouth is a mouse'. Must include: scroll the screen and any pane; scroll tables and grids; select a row, multi-select rows, select all/none; right-click / open the context menu on any element or row; pick a context menu item by its spoken label; open submenus and pick submenu items; type into and read every field (inputs, notes, selects, switches, checkboxes, sliders); save/cancel/close dialogs; drag and drop, resize, reorder; hover-only and long-press actions; tabs, toolbars, banners, nav and app menus. Every result reports what actually changed on screen, not just 'delivered'. Same through REST, MCP, CLI and voice. CI check fails on any UI element with no voice/API address. Run after the axHub + AmberX move lands.
Split by Claude into 18 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: The API needs to fully control everything. The API needs to be able to drive the entire app.

steps.text: Design the field address contract: add field:<dialog|screen>/<name> and dialog submit/cancel to console-control (get/set value semantics per control kind: text, textarea, select, switch, checkbox, number, radio; value coercion; error codes for unknown field or bad value; action-args fill-then-save rule for new:<title>). Update CONSOLE-CONTROL.md and the control address schema.

Engine: add field address parsing, value coercion and validation to the console-control core engine (pure, no DOM), plus golden fixtures for every control kind and error case; record the Android twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.

Framework controls register field targets by themselves: TextField, TextArea, SelectField, Switch, Checkbox, Segmented and NumberField take a name and emit data-axf-target=field:<scope>/<name>, with the scope taken from the enclosing Dialog/View context, so a plugin never wires it by hand.

Runtime field driver: set/get on a field target writes through React's value setter and fires the input/change events (controlled inputs update their state), reads the current value, and dialog submit/cancel presses the dialog's primary or cancel action. Unit test with jsdom.

Console server: REST /api/console-control gets field.get, field.set (one or many fields in one call) and dialog.submit/cancel, routed to the open browser session with the same relay as press; refuses personOnly and owner-only settings.
MCP tools console_control_field_get, console_control_field_set and console_control_dialog_submit in mcp_server.py, matching the REST shapes; add them to the console tools pin.
CLI: axf console field get|set <address> [value] and axf console submit <dialog>, with --json for several fields at once.
Voice (AmberX): intents 'set <field> to <value>', 'type <text> into <field>', 'tick/untick <checkbox>', 'save' resolve to field addresses via the Ctrl+K search index.

Action args fill forms: a console action that opens a dialog with args (new:<title>, rename:<text>) fills the named fields from the args and saves. Add the generic args-to-fields map to the action registry.

Plan Studio 2.0: the Plan item dialog's Title, Note, Kind, Priority, Model and checkbox fields get names. plan-studio-2.new and new-inside fill the title and note from args and save; rename takes text; note, priority and model are settable on an existing item.

Plan Studio 2.0 API parity: plugin commands new, new-inside, rename, note, priority, model and tick take values over REST, MCP (plugin-commands), CLI and voice, each with a deep link that opens the item; README section.

CI check check-console-control-fields.mjs: statically finds every input, textarea, select, switch and checkbox (raw or framework control) in the console and plugins without a settable field address; ratchet baseline that only goes down. Wire it into CI.
Sweep 1: name the form controls in Settings and its plugin sub-tabs (setting: addresses get field aliases) and lower the baseline.
Sweep 2: builds plugins (build-orchestrator, pipeline, gate, plan-studio, ui-review) dialogs and forms get named fields; lower the baseline.

Sweep 3: agent-swarm, claude-settings, claude-session, notify-control, codebase-changes, theme-manager and the rest of the plugins; lower the baseline toward zero, recording any control that truly cannot be addressed with a reason.
Sweep 4: console core views (Terminal, Breakroom, Home, dialogs in framework/react such as chrome settings and asset pickers); re-bake src/axf; baseline at its final count.

End-to-end test: with Playwright against a preview console, create a nested Plan Studio 2.0 plan (parent plus two children) with titles, notes, priority and ticked checkboxes entirely through REST, then MCP, then the CLI. Verify on screen via field.get and a screenshot to UI Review Screenshots (group named after the build).

Tests, report and PR: run check-console-control, check-console-control-fields, fixtures, the server tests and the e2e. Write _claude/builds/reports/api-fully-drives-every-field-type-forms.md (how each feature is reached via deep link, state, actions, REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Update the docs/console-control.md, add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR.

Console server: REST /api/console-control gets field.get, field.set (one or many fields in one call) and dialog.submit/cancel, routed to the open browser session with the same relay as press; refuses personOnly and owner-only settings.
MCP tools console_control_field_get, console_control_field_set and console_control_dialog_submit in mcp_server.py, matching the REST shapes; add them to the console tools pin.
CLI: axf console field get|set <address> [value] and axf console submit <dialog>, with --json for several fields at once.
Voice (AmberX): intents 'set <field> to <value>', 'type <text> into <field>', 'tick/untick <checkbox>', 'save' resolve to field addresses via the Ctrl+K search index.

Action args fill forms: a console action that opens a dialog with args (new:<title>, rename:<text>) fills the named fields from the args and saves. Add the generic args-to-fields map to the action registry.

Plan Studio 2.0: the Plan item dialog's Title, Note, Kind, Priority, Model and checkbox fields get names. plan-studio-2.new and new-inside fill the title and note from args and save; rename takes text; note, priority and model are settable on an existing item.

Sweep 2: builds plugins (build-orchestrator, pipeline, gate, plan-studio, ui-review) dialogs and forms get named fields; lower the baseline.

Sweep 3: agent-swarm, claude-settings, claude-session, notify-control, codebase-changes, theme-manager and the rest of the plugins; lower the baseline toward zero, recording any control that truly cannot be addressed with a reason.
Sweep 4: console core views (Terminal, Breakroom, Home, dialogs in framework/react such as chrome settings and asset pickers); re-bake src/axf; baseline at its final count.

End-to-end test: with Playwright against a preview console, create a nested Plan Studio 2.0 plan (parent plus two children) with titles, notes, priority and ticked checkboxes entirely through REST, then MCP, then the CLI. Verify on screen via field.get and a screenshot to UI Review Screenshots (group named after the build).

Write _claude/builds/reports/api-fully-drives-every-field-type-forms.md (how each feature is reached via deep link, state, actions, REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Update the docs/console-control.md, add the THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR.

Design the field address contract: add field:<dialog|screen>/<name> and dialog submit/cancel to console-control (get/set value semantics per control kind: text, textarea, select, switch, checkbox, number, radio; value coercion; error codes for unknown field or bad value; action-args fill-then-save rule for new:<title>). Update CONSOLE-CONTROL.md and the control address schema.

Engine: add field address parsing, value coercion and validation to the console-control core engine (pure, no DOM), plus golden fixtures for every control kind and error case; record the Android twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md.

Framework controls register field targets by themselves: TextField, TextArea, SelectField, Switch, Checkbox, Segmented and NumberField take a name and emit data-axf-target=field:<scope>/<name>, with the scope taken from the enclosing Dialog/View context, so a plugin never wires it by hand.

Runtime field driver: set/get on a field target writes through React's value setter and fires the input/change events (controlled inputs update their state), reads the current value, and dialog submit/cancel presses the dialog's primary or cancel action. Unit test with jsdom.

Console server: REST /api/console-control gets field.get, field.set (one or many fields in one call) and dialog.submit/cancel, routed to the open browser session with the same relay as press; refuses personOnly and owner-only settings.
MCP tools console_control_field_get, console_control_field_set and console_control_dialog_submit in mcp_server.py, matching the REST shapes; add them to the console tools pin.
CLI: axf console field get|set <address> [value] and axf console submit <dialog>, with --json for several fields at once.
Voice (AmberX): intents 'set <field> to <value>', 'type <text> into <field>', 'tick/untick <checkbox>', 'save' resolve to field addresses via the Ctrl+K search index.

Action args fill forms: a console action that opens a dialog with args (new:<title>, rename:<text>) fills the named fields from the args and saves. Add the generic args-to-fields map to the action registry.
